title: Vowels — Long and Short
subtitle: Nine vowels. Length is phonemic.
objectives: Distinguish long vowels from short vowels by sight and sound.
Pronounce y and ø correctly (front rounded vowels).
Understand that vowel length distinguishes meaning: mál ≠ mal.

sections.heading: The nine vowels
sections.body:
Old Norse has nine vowel qualities: a, e, i, o, u, y, æ, ø, ǫ. Each (except æ, which is always long) can be short or long. Long vowels are marked with an acute accent in modern editions: á, é, í, ó, ú, ý. Ø can be written ö in some editions; we use ø to avoid confusion with ǫ.

Length is phonemic. Mál (speech) and mal (bag) are different words. Fór (went) and for (before) are different words. You must train your ear to hear the difference and your eye to see the accent mark.

letters.name: y (short)
letters.note: High front rounded. As in French tu or German ü.

letters.name: ø
letters.note: Mid front rounded. As in French peu or German ö.

sections.heading: Y and ø — front rounded vowels
sections.body:
English has no front rounded vowels. French and German do. Y = high front rounded (like French tu, German über). Ø = mid front rounded (like French peu, German schön).

To pronounce y: say English ee as in see, then round your lips without moving your tongue. To pronounce ø: say English ay as in say, then round your lips.

Common words with y: mýrr (mire), dýr (animal), fyr (fire). Common words with ø: øx (axe), søkkva (to sink), øl (ale — but also spelled ǫl).

sections.heading: Listening drill — long vs short
sections.instructions: Listen to pairs of words that differ only in vowel length. Repeat each pair.

items.prompt: What is the difference between mál and mal?
items.answer: Vowel length. Mál (long á) = speech. Mal (short a) = bag.
Say ee (as in see), then round your lips. High front rounded vowel, as in French tu.
Say ay (as in say), then round your lips. Mid front rounded vowel, as in French peu.

items.prompt: Is vowel length phonemic in Old Norse?
